arxiv-2108-11766.title: Minimally doubled fermions and topology in 2D This talk is devoted to the memory of Prof. Artan Boriçi (19.4.1965-25.3.2021) who fell victim to the covid pandemic.
arxiv-2108-11766.creator: *, Johannes H. Weber
arxiv-2108-11766.description: Abstract We use the two-dimensional Schwinger model to investigate how lattice fermions perceive the global topological charge q ∈ 𝐙 q\in\mathbf{Z} of a given gauge background U U . After a warm-up part devoted to staggered, Adams, Wilson and naive fermions, we consider Karsten-Wilczek and Boriçi-Creutz fermions, which are in the class of minimally doubled lattice fermion actions.

arxiv-2111-13605.title: A NOVEL GPR-BASED PREDICTION MODEL FOR CYCLIC BACKBONE CURVES OF REINFORCED CONCRETE SHEAR WALLS
arxiv-2111-13605.creator: Zeynep Tuna Deger, Ph.D, Gulsen Taskin Kaya, Ph.D
arxiv-2111-13605.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zeynep Tuna Deger, Ph.D, Gulsen Taskin Kaya, Ph.D. Backbone curves are used to characterize nonlinear responses of structural elements by simplifying the cyclic force – deformation relationships. Accurate modeling of cyclic behavior can be achieved with a reliable backbone curve model. In this paper, a novel machine learning-based model is proposed to predict the backbone curve of reinforced concrete shear (structural) walls based on key wall design properties.

arxiv-2205-01655.title: Effective Field Theory Islands from Perturbative and Nonperturbative Four-Graviton Amplitudes
arxiv-2205-01655.creator: Zvi Bern, Enrico Herrmann, Dimitrios Kosmopoulos, Radu Roiban
arxiv-2205-01655.description: Abstract Theoretical data obtained from physically sensible field and string theory models suggest that gravitational Effective Field Theories (EFTs) live on islands that are tiny compared to current general bounds determined from unitarity, causality, crossing symmetry, and a good high-energy behavior.

arxiv-2207-03699.title: Tightening Discretization-based MILP Models for the Pooling Problem using Upper Bounds on Bilinear Terms
arxiv-2207-03699.creator: Yifu Chen, Christos T. Maravelias, Xiaomin Zhang
arxiv-2207-03699.description: Abstract Discretization-based methods have been proposed for solving nonconvex optimization problems with bilinear terms such as the pooling problem. These methods convert the original nonconvex optimization problems into mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs). In this paper we study tightening methods for these MILP models for the pooling problem, and derive valid constraints using upper bounds on bilinear terms.

arxiv-2212-11409.title: DExT: Detector Explanation Toolkit
arxiv-2212-11409.creator: Deepan Chakravarthi Padmanabhan, Paul G. Plöger, Octavio Arriaga, Matias Valdenegro-Toro
arxiv-2212-11409.description: Abstract State-of-the-art object detectors are treated as black boxes due to their highly non-linear internal computations. Even with unprecedented advancements in detector performance, the inability to explain how their outputs are generated limits their use in safety-critical applications. Previous work fails to produce explanations for both bounding box and classification decisions, and generally make individual explanations for various detectors.

In this paper, we introduce the concepts of short arc and length map in quasihyperbolic metric spaces, and obtain some geometric characterizations of Gromov hyperbolicity for quasihyperbolic metric spaces in terms of the properties of short arc and length map. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 30C65, 30F45; Secondary: 30L10. 1.

arxiv-2503-21667.title: The Construction of Asymptotic Bode Plots: A New Direct Method
arxiv-2503-21667.creator: Davide Tebaldi, Roberto Zanasi
arxiv-2503-21667.description: Abstract Bode plots represent an essential tool in control and systems engineering. In order to perform an initial qualitative analysis of the considered systems, the construction of asymptotic Bode plots is often sufficient. The standard methods for constructing asymptotic Bode plots are characterized by the same drawbacks: they are not systematic, may be not precise and time-consuming.

arxiv-2511-17025.title: Comparison of linear observation techniques for robust load torque estimation in actuators
arxiv-2511-17025.creator: Michael Ruderman, Elia Brescia, Luigi P. Savastio, Paolo R. Massenio, David Naso, Giuseppe L. Cascella
arxiv-2511-17025.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Michael Ruderman, Elia Brescia, Luigi P. Savastio, Paolo R. Massenio, David Naso, Giuseppe L. Cascella. The paper addresses the problem of estimating robustly the external load torque in rotary actuator systems, when only the generated motor drive torque and angular displacement are the available input and output. We compare, theoretically and experimentally, two sufficiently established linear observation techniques (i) reduced-order Luenberger observer and (ii) disturbance observer, both using the same identified model of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM)-based actuator.

pmc-12427535.creator: Gabriela Studer, Tino Streller, David Jeller, Dirk Huebner, Bruno Fuchs, Christoph Glanzmann
pmc-12427535.description: Simple SummaryLattice Radiation Therapy (LRT), a spatially fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy (SBRT) technique, has shown promising results in the palliative treatment of large tumors. The focus of our first analysis of 56 lesions ≥7 cm was on the extent of shrinkage following palliative LRT.

pmc-12528494.title: A lightweight blockchain based scalable and collaborative mitigation framework against new flow DDoS attacks in SDN enabled autonomous systems
pmc-12528494.creator: Shikha Garg, Sonia Goyal, Abhinav Bhandari
pmc-12528494.description: The New-flow based DDoS attacks are new kinds of attacks that pose a severe threat to SDN-Enabled AS by exploiting vulnerabilities of the centralized SDN controller. This research paper proposes the lightweight blockchain-based framework for Scalable and Collaborative DDoS Mitigation in SDN-Enabled Autonomous Systems (LiBSCOM-AS).

pmc-12541521.title: Current management strategies for bladder neck stenosis and vesicourethral anastomotic stenosis
pmc-12541521.creator: Benjamin M Mac Curtain, Behzad Abbasi, Adrian M Fernandez, Lynn Leng, Marvin Carlisle, Benjamin N Breyer
pmc-12541521.description: Bladder neck stenosis (BNS) and vesicourethral anastomotic stenosis (VUAS) are forms of posterior urethral narrowing, typically resulting from benign prostate surgery and radical prostatectomy, respectively. Cystoscopy confirms the diagnosis, while voiding cystourethrography and retrograde urethrogram help assess disease extent. Magnetic resonance imaging may be useful in evaluating complex or previously irradiated patients.

pmc-12649098.title: Molecular effects of transposable element sequences in mammalian cells
pmc-12649098.creator: Ming-Ching C Wen, Joshua D Welch
pmc-12649098.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Transposable elements (TEs) are often epigenetically repressed in eukaryotic cells, but still affect the molecular state of the cell in certain contexts. A flurry of recent studies have elucidated new effects of TE sequences in eukaryotic cells. We review these emerging molecular effects of TEs, including a variety of new mechanisms by which TE sequences affect the cell, including pre- and post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression; cell-to-cell transmission of genes within a multicellular organism through virus-like activity; and RNA-guided DNA insertion.

pmc-13066348.title: Impact of preoperative biliary drainage on surgical risk in pancreaticoduodenectomy for resectable periampullary tumors
pmc-13066348.creator: Huajun Lin, Boyu Deng, Chenglin Xin, Peixin Li, Ying Jian, Xiaoya Yu, Tianyi Wang, Dong Wang
pmc-13066348.description: BackgroundPancreaticoduodenectomy (PD), as a challenging surgical procedure, is associated with considerable morbidity and mortality rates. Currently, the impact of preoperative biliary drainage (PBD) on the surgical risk of PD remains controversial. Therefore, we conducted a retrospective cohort study to analyze factors influencing the surgical risk of PD and to evaluate the role of biliary drainage therein.

pmc-13092255.title: Effects of Ciprofol Combined with Varying Doses of Alfentanil on Anesthetic Efficacy and Safety in Pediatric Bronchoscopy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13092255.creator: Qiao Yang, Weihua He, Fan Li, Shenglong Bi, Qiong Jiang
pmc-13092255.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate the anesthetic safety of the ciprofol and alfentanil regimen for pediatric bronchoscopy and to determine the effective concentration of alfentanil.MethodsIn this single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial, pediatric patients scheduled for fiberoptic bronchoscopy were randomly divided into three groups: ciprofol combined with 5 μg/kg alfentanil group (Group A), ciprofol combined with 10 μg/kg alfentanil group (Group B) and ciprofol-only group (Group C).

pmc-13265912.title: ‌An mRNA vaccine confers enhanced protection against herpes simplex virus through an IFN-I-dependent pathway
pmc-13265912.creator: Wenying Zhao, Lingjin Sun, Peng Wang, Qian Zhao, Ying Li, Yang Li, Hongyang Shi, Man Xing, Weiqian Dai, Dongming Zhou
pmc-13265912.description: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) types 1 and 2 cause widespread oral or genital infections, but no prophylactic or therapeutic HSV vaccine has been approved to date. In this study, we developed three mRNA vaccine candidates expressing key viral glycoproteins: monovalent gD2, bivalent gD2-gC1, and bivalent gD2-gE1. We assessed their immunogenicity and protective efficacy in a murine model.

pmc-13454600.title: Automated leukemia detection from microscopic images using deep transfer learning with explainable AI-based analysis
pmc-13454600.creator: Md Ashikuzzaman, Mir Md. Julhash, Md. Feroz Ali, Md Shafiul Alam, Mohammad Ali, Imil Hamda Imran, Obaidullah Obaidi, Md Kamrul Islam
pmc-13454600.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Leukemia, a life-threatening hematological malignancy, necessitates early and accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. Traditional microscopic examination is often time-consuming and subjective, while most existing deep learning-based studies are limited to a narrow selection of models and lack interpretability analysis. To address these gaps, this study presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of fourteen pre-trained CNN architectures, including EfficientNetB1/B3/B5, Xception, InceptionV3, InceptionResNetV2, DenseNet201, ResNet variants, VGG16/19, and MobileNet, for automated leukemia detection from microscopic blood smear images.

pmc-13566138.title: Population Decline May Affect the Incidence of Pulmonary Tuberculosis in Japan
pmc-13566138.creator: Akihiro Miyauchi, Mizuki Inaba, Takatoshi Tetsuka, Noritaka Sakamoto, Yushi Nomura, Otohiro Katsube, Hirokuni Hirata, Hiroshige Yoshioka, Seiji Niho, Kumiya Sugiyama
pmc-13566138.description: Background/Objectives: Pulmonary tuberculosis in Japan had been decreasing as a result of the country’s anti-tuberculosis policy. The decreased number of patients with tuberculosis has led to many tuberculosis units being downsized. However, the decreasing trend in incidence ended in 2022. To resume this trend, it is important to clarify which populations are at higher risk of developing tuberculosis.
